findings.title: A scent leads the return
findings.claim: The caravan's departure opens an interval in which Yusuf's scent reaches his father before the bearers do. The later contact, restored sight, petition, and return of the family make the scent an early, contested sign within a larger movement from separation toward reunion.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins the setting-out verb to a provision-bearing caravan, the father's sensory finding, and the anticipated charge of weakened judgment. The caravan noun also carries an accepted reproach and ill-repute branch; the focus's feared discredit and the immediate reply activate it as a secondary contextual echo, while the ordinary caravan sense remains intact. The reply in 12:95 enacts that charge; 12:96 supplies bodily contact and visual confirmation; 12:97 turns the former judges into petitioners. The family estrangement named at 12:100 also activates the focus departure's general separation facet, while the scent crosses that narrative gap. This changes the event from a private smell report into the first link of a sign-and-return sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the scent matters before the caravan arrives: it makes an absent person actionable, even while the family disputes the perceiver. The caravan's name also picks up a restrained echo of the reproach that follows.
findings.containment: This does not establish how the scent physically traveled, make the object cast onto the father's face carry the same odor, or prove that the departure itself causes the family estrangement. The caravan's reproach branch remains a secondary root resonance, not its ordinary meaning. The two fanad readings are source-nominated images supported here by the immediate response and its old-error wording.

epistemic.reason: The focus wording and pericope sequence are directly supplied. The blame and senility images are trusted channel nominations; the caravan's accepted reproach branch is noted upstream only as secondary sound pressure, and its contextual activation remains bounded.
